taxonomy.subtopic: Right ventricular outflow obstruction and hypercyanotic spells

questions.stem_html:
A 3-year-old boy with a harsh systolic murmur becomes deeply cyanotic and tachypneic while crying. He instinctively squats and improves within minutes. Echocardiography shows a ventricular septal defect, an overriding aorta, right ventricular hypertrophy, and severe infundibular pulmonary stenosis.

How does squatting improve this episode?

options.text_html: Increasing systemic vascular resistance reduces right-to-left flow across the ventricular septal defect
Decreasing venous return lowers right ventricular filling and improves pulmonary blood flow
Lowering pulmonary vascular resistance closes the ventricular septal defect
Increasing heart rate shortens the duration of right-to-left shunting
Dilating the aorta diverts more blood into the pulmonary artery

questions.explanation_html: Squatting compresses systemic arteries and raises systemic vascular resistance. This increases left ventricular pressure relative to the right, reducing right-to-left shunting through the VSD and directing more blood toward the pulmonary circulation. Hypercyanotic spells worsen when right ventricular outflow obstruction and low systemic resistance favor right-to-left shunting; squatting reverses that pressure relationship.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Squatting tends to increase venous return and systemic resistance; reducing preload is not the therapeutic mechanism.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: The VSD does not acutely close, and pulmonary flow improves mainly because systemic resistance opposes right-to-left shunting.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Tachycardia can worsen a hypercyanotic spell by reducing filling time and increasing dynamic outflow obstruction.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Aortic dilation would not selectively restore pulmonary flow in Tetralogy of Fallot.

questions.educational_objective: Explain why squatting relieves a Tetralogy of Fallot spell by increasing systemic vascular resistance and reducing right-to-left shunting.
